purpose: Cefpodoxime is an antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including ear infections, sinus infections, throat infections, bronchitis, pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and certain skin infections. It works only against bacteria, so it will not help with viral infections like the common cold or flu. Always finish the full course your doctor prescribed, even if you start feeling better sooner.
how_it_works: Cefpodoxime works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria, which bacteria need to survive. Without this protective wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. Think of it like removing the outer shell that holds the bacteria together — once it is gone, the bacteria cannot survive.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, stomach upset, and headache. Some people may notice a mild skin rash. Taking the medication with food can help reduce stomach upset. If you develop severe or watery diarrhea, contact your doctor, as this can sometimes indicate a more serious gut infection.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotics, as there is a small chance of a related allergic reaction. Stop taking it and seek emergency help right away if you develop hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, especially antacids or stomach acid reducers, because they can reduce how well this antibiotic is absorbed. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 100 mg to 200 mg taken by mouth every 12 hours (twice a day), usually for 5 to 14 days depending on the infection being treated. It is best taken with food to help your body absorb it better and to reduce stomach upset. For children, the dose is based on their weight, so always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions.
